intro: To change where Zoom saves local recordings on a Mac, open Settings in the Zoom Workplace desktop app, choose the Recording tab, and click Change next to Storage location. Then pick a folder on your Mac's own drive with free space, and record a short test to confirm the new path works.
tldr: Open Settings from your profile picture in the Zoom Workplace desktop app.
Go to the Recording tab, then click Change next to Storage location.
The default folder on a Mac is /Users/[Username]/Documents/Zoom.
The web portal cannot change the local path, and admins control cloud storage.
Pick a folder on your Mac's own drive, then test one recording before a real meeting.

blocks.text: Zoom saves local recordings to a folder on your Mac, and you choose which folder that is. The setting lives in the desktop app, not in the web portal. Once you know where it sits, the change takes a few clicks. The rest of this page covers what goes wrong after the change, from network drives to disk space, so you can avoid those problems.
Change the recording folder step by step on Mac

The steps in this guide use the Zoom Workplace desktop app for macOS. Zoom's desktop app was renamed from the Zoom app to Zoom Workplace, as an April 18, 2024 post from SMU ITconnect explains. Older articles may still use the old name. Some guides also label the field differently. Use the labels on your own screen, and follow the order below.
Before you start

items: Sign in to the Zoom Workplace desktop app on the Mac that makes the recording. The web portal cannot change the local path.
Check that your account can make computer recordings. Zoom's notes say a Basic account or above is required.
Create the destination folder in Finder first, so you can pick it in one step.
Stop any recording in progress, so you do not change the folder mid-capture.
Write down the current folder. You will need it if you go looking for older files.

blocks.text: If the profile picture route does not match your screen, look for a gear icon in the navigation bar. Zoom's settings article says that icon opens Settings in versions 6.7.0 and higher. If your version does not show the icon, use the profile picture route instead.
Where your recordings are saved right now

Find the folder you use today before you move anything. On a Mac, the default computer recording folder is /Users/[Username]/Documents/Zoom. Replace [Username] with your macOS account name. The Storage location field shows the folder Zoom is using, and the Open button opens that folder so you can look inside.

Do not assume that changing the folder moves your old files. The Zoom support pages behind this guide do not say whether existing recordings move with the new setting. After the change, check the old folder. Copy anything you need somewhere safe before you delete the old folder, because a deleted folder is hard to get back.
Why the web portal cannot change the path

If you look for this setting in the Zoom web portal, you will not find it. The portal only lists computer recordings. Go to Recordings & Transcripts, then open the Computer recordings tab. A Location column shows where each file lives on the computer.
Playback works only on the device where the recording was made. That makes the Location column the one to trust when you hunt for a file. Check it before you assume a file is lost.

Cloud recordings follow a different rule. Admins set the Recordings and content location under Admin Center, then Settings, General, and Data & Storage. If you use a Business or Enterprise account, you cannot view or change that location yourself, so ask your admin first.
Pick a folder that will not fail mid-meeting

The folder has to be a valid local path with room to write. Zoom's troubleshooting article ties an invalid path to a bad network connection. Its storage article warns that a path not physically on your device, such as a network drive, can cause problems. A network drive can drop for a moment, and that alone can break a recording.

items: Good: a folder inside Documents on the Mac's internal drive.
Good, with care: an external drive that stays plugged in for every meeting.
Risky: a network drive or file server, because a dropped connection can stop a recording.

blocks.text: Disk space is the other common failure. Zoom lists Error Code 614 for a computer that may be low on disk space when it records. Check the drive that holds the folder, not only the startup disk, because your folder may live somewhere else.
Fix the errors that show up after you change it

Zoom's troubleshooting notes cover the problems below, and each one has a different cause. Match the message on your screen before you change anything else. The table lists each case with the fix Zoom's notes give.

rows: The recording path is invalid, or the network connection to it dropped
Pick a valid local folder in Storage location, then record again
The computer may be low on disk space while recording
Free space on the drive, delete files you no longer need, then record again
Recording not found at the listed path
The file is not where Zoom expected it
Check the Location field under Computer recordings in the web portal
Double-click does nothing on a .zoom file
The file is a double_click_to_convert file that needs conversion
Read the Transcode section below, and contact Zoom support first
blocks.caption: Common recording errors and the fix Zoom's support pages give.

blocks.text: Error Code 614 is about space, not the folder. Free room on the drive, then delete old files you no longer need. Do this before the next meeting, not during it. Zoom's notes do not give a minimum amount of free space, so leave plenty of headroom.
Convert a .zoom file on a Mac

Some local recordings arrive as double_click_to_convert_01.zoom files. Zoom's troubleshooting article says that double-clicking one can do nothing on a Mac. Its manual workaround copies Transcode from the zoom.us package, in Contents and Frameworks, into Applications. Then, in Get Info, you set Open with to Transcode and double-click the file.
Two warnings apply. Renaming those files during conversion may corrupt them. The workaround also touches app files, so ask Zoom support before you try it, and keep a copy of the recording first.
Windows paths look different from the Mac path

Zoom's file directory article gives the local recording path only in Windows format. It starts with the system drive, then Users, your user name, and the Documents and Zoom folders. It gives no Mac path. On your Mac, use /Users/[Username]/Documents/Zoom and the Settings steps above. If you support both platforms, write the two paths down separately so nobody mixes them up.
A worked example: moving recordings to a new folder

Say you record client calls and want them in a folder called Client Recordings inside Documents. Create that folder in Finder first. Then open Settings from the profile picture, go to Recording, and click Change next to Storage location. Choose Client Recordings and check the Storage location field.

Next, record a short test by yourself. A test shows more than the settings screen does. Open the folder with the Open button and confirm the file is there. If it is missing, read the errors table before you schedule the next client call.
Mistakes people make with the recording folder

items: Picking a network drive because it has the most free space.
Changing the folder in the middle of a meeting, then searching for the file later.
Deleting the old folder before checking whether anything is still in it.
Looking for the setting in the web portal, which only shows where files are.
Assuming a cloud storage location is the same thing as the local folder.
Skipping the test recording, and finding out about a problem during a real call.

blocks.text: Keyboard shortcuts and menu labels

Zoom's support pages for this flow do not list a keyboard shortcut, so this guide does not give one. The steps use mouse or trackpad clicks only. The Settings window holds 13 tabs in the desktop app, from General to My account, so read the tab names before you click.
Version notes and what Zoom does not say

Zoom Workplace is the current name for the desktop app. Zoom's computer recording article gives no numeric minimum version for macOS. It only says the desktop app must be at the Global minimum version or higher. If your Settings window looks different from these steps, check for an update in the app.

A third-party tracker lists recent Zoom Workplace macOS builds, but Zoom's consolidated release notes page does not list version numbers. Treat tracker data as a guess. The steps on this page follow the menu labels, not a build number.

Once the folder is set and your test recording is safe, the next thing to check is your screen share. The guide to [sharing your screen in Zoom on Mac](/how-to/share-your-screen-in-zoom) covers the desktop steps and the black screen fixes.

faq.question: Can I change the recording location in Zoom on Mac from the web portal?
faq.answer: No. The web portal shows where each computer recording is saved in its Location column, but it cannot change the local path on your Mac. Make the change in the Zoom Workplace desktop app under Settings, then Recording.

faq.question: Where does Zoom save recordings on a Mac by default?
faq.answer: The default computer recording folder is /Users/[Username]/Documents/Zoom. Replace [Username] with your macOS account name. Click Open in the Recording tab to see the folder Zoom is using now.

faq.question: Why does Zoom say Invalid working path or folder?
faq.answer: The recording path is invalid, or the connection to it dropped. Zoom's support article says a dropped network connection can trigger the error. Pick a valid local folder in Storage location and try again.

faq.question: What does Error Code 614 mean for my recordings?
faq.answer: Zoom says the computer may have low disk space when the recording runs. Check free space on the drive that holds the folder, delete files you no longer need, and record again. Zoom does not give a minimum amount of free space.

faq.question: Can my admin change where Zoom saves cloud recordings?
faq.answer: Yes. Admins set Recordings and content location under Admin Center, then Settings, General, and Data & Storage. Individual users on Business or Enterprise accounts cannot view or change that location.

faq.question: Do old recordings move when I change the folder?
faq.answer: The Zoom support pages behind this guide do not say that they move. Check the old folder after the change. Copy anything you need before you delete the old folder.

faq.question: Why does a recording play on one computer but not another?
faq.answer: Zoom says playback works only on the device where the recording was made. Test playback on the Mac that made the file, and do not assume a copy will play somewhere else.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut to change the recording location?
faq.answer: Zoom's support pages for this flow do not list one, so this guide does not give one. Use the mouse or trackpad path in the steps above.

task: Change the local recording folder in Zoom on Mac
requirements: Zoom Workplace desktop app for macOS, signed in
A Basic account or above for computer recordings
A destination folder on your Mac's internal drive or a drive that stays connected
Enough free disk space for the meetings you plan to record

steps.name: Open the Zoom Workplace desktop app
steps.text: Open Zoom Workplace on your Mac and sign in. The change happens in the desktop app. The web portal cannot change the local recording path, so skip the browser for this part.

steps.name: Click your profile picture
steps.text: Look at the top right of the app window and click your profile picture. A menu opens. If your version shows a gear icon in the navigation bar, you can click that instead.
steps.tip: Zoom's settings article says the gear icon opens Settings in versions 6.7.0 and higher.

steps.name: Open Settings
steps.text: In the menu, click Settings. The Settings window opens with a list of tabs. It holds 13 tabs in total, from General to My account.

steps.name: Click the Recording tab
steps.text: In the Settings tabs, click Recording. This tab holds the default local recording storage location. The other tabs do not hold this setting.

steps.name: Find Local recording storage
steps.text: Scroll to the section called Local recording storage. Look for the field labeled Storage location. It shows the folder Zoom uses now, such as the default Documents/Zoom folder.

steps.name: Click Change
steps.text: Click Change next to Storage location. Zoom's article says Change lets you pick a new location, but it does not describe the dialog, so follow what appears on your screen.
steps.tip: Create the new folder in Finder before you click Change, so it is ready to select.

steps.name: Choose the new folder
steps.text: Select the folder you want, then confirm the choice in the dialog. Pick a folder on your Mac's internal drive, or a drive that stays plugged in. Avoid network drives, because Zoom's storage article warns about paths that are not on your device.
steps.tip: Use a folder name you will recognize later, such as Client Recordings.

steps.name: Check the Storage location field
steps.text: Look at the Storage location field again. It should show the new path. If it still shows the old one, repeat the Change step and choose the folder again.

steps.name: Open the folder to confirm
steps.text: Click Open next to the field to view the folder. Confirm that it is the folder you chose. This check takes seconds and catches a wrong pick before a meeting.

steps.name: Record a short test
steps.text: Start a test meeting, record for a short time, and stop. Then open the new folder and check that the recording is there. If Zoom shows an error, read the troubleshooting list on this page before the next meeting.

troubleshooting.fix: Choose a valid local folder under Storage location. If the path is on a network drive, move it to a folder on your Mac, then record again.
Free disk space on the drive that holds the recording folder. Delete or move old files, then record again before the meeting.

troubleshooting.problem: A recording is not in the folder Zoom lists
troubleshooting.fix: Sign in to the web portal, go to Recordings & Transcripts, then Computer recordings. Find the meeting ID and read the Location field.

troubleshooting.problem: Deleting a row in the web portal seems to remove the file
troubleshooting.fix: Removing a row only removes it from the list. The file stays on the computer, so check the folder in Finder.
Do not rename the file. Read the Transcode workaround on this page, and ask Zoom support before you copy any app files.
